subject: Architecture
title: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge: Earthquake Survivor
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge: Earthquake Survivor.

hook.text: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge spans 6,532 feet — nearly a mile and a quarter — the longest suspension span.

buildup.text: Two towers rise 928 feet above sea level, supporting cables containing 300,000 miles of steel wire.

discovery.text: During construction, the 1995 Kobe earthquake shifted the two towers three feet farther apart.

twist.text: Engineers had built in enough tolerance. They simply adjusted the deck design to fit the new span length.

climax.text: Tuned mass dampers and pendulums in each tower counteract typhoon winds and earthquake forces.

punchline.text: An earthquake moved the bridge. The bridge didn't care.

quiz.question: What happened to the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge during the 1995 Kobe earthquake?
options: One tower partially collapsed and was rebuilt
The towers shifted three feet apart, and the design was adjusted
The main cables snapped and had to be replaced

details.summary: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge in Japan held the world's longest span record at 1,991 meters from its 1998 opening until 2022. During construction, the 1995 Kobe earthquake shifted the towers apart by a full meter, forcing engineers to redesign the deck panels to accommodate the changed geometry.
details.whyItMatters: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge demonstrates engineering resilience — surviving a major earthquake during construction and adapting without starting over.
takeaways: Held the world's longest span record at 1,991 meters until 2022
The 1995 Kobe earthquake shifted its towers one meter apart
Engineers redesigned panels to accommodate the shifted geometry

faq.question: How did the bridge survive the Kobe earthquake?
faq.answer: The towers were founded on massive caissons sunk into bedrock that withstood the magnitude 6.9 quake. While the earthquake moved the towers one meter further apart, the flexible cable system accommodated the shift. Engineers adjusted the unstalled deck panels for the new span length.

faq.question: How does the bridge handle typhoon winds?
faq.answer: Pendulum-like tuned mass dampers inside each tower counteract wind-induced swaying. The stiffening truss deck was designed with aerodynamic openings to let wind pass through rather than push against it. The bridge can withstand winds up to 286 kilometers per hour.
